site.title: Kelly Marie Counselling | Leeds Psychotherapist
site.description: Kelly Marie Counselling - BACP-registered psychotherapist based in Leeds offering individual, workplace, group therapy - online and in person.

hero.paragraph1: Evidence-based psychotherapy and counselling for organisations, individuals and groups — delivered with confidence, face-to-face, online and within the workplace.
hero.paragraph2: Whether you are facing anxiety, depression, relationship difficulties, trauma or a significant life transition, I provide structured clinical support grounded in psychodynamic and integrative practice.

about.paragraph1: I'm Kelly Marie, a BACP-registered psychotherapist based in Leeds with over a decade of clinical experience working with individuals, couples, young people and organisations. I am a proud advocate for wellbeing and mental health awareness.
about.paragraph2: My practice is grounded in psychodynamic theory - drawing on how early relational experiences and unconscious patterns shape our present-day emotional lives. Working alongside integrative and trauma-informed approaches, I offer a thoughtful, evidence-based and confidential service that's tailored to your clinical needs.
about.paragraph3: I specialise in workplace therapy and wellbeing, working with organisations. As a contracted therapist within an organisation, I work closely with HR and management teams to prioritise mental health and wellbeing in the workplace. This is to ensure that employees that may benefit from my services are referred promptly and given the right support.

services.heading: How I Can Help
services.intro: My mission is to prioritise mental health and wellbeing across the UK. I offer a safe space and empower individuals to take proactive and sustainable steps towards improved mental health.

cards.title: Workplace Wellbeing
cards.description: Confidential therapeutic support and wellbeing consultancy for organisations. Employee assistance, stress management programmes and leadership resilience — delivered on-site or remotely. Workplace therapy aims to reduce staff absence due to psychological health, support the phased return of employees and implement a human-centered working culture.

cards.title: Group Sessions
cards.description: Structured group therapy programmes harnessing the therapeutic value of shared experience. Facilitated groups for anxiety, grief and personal development run throughout the year.

cards.title: Remote Sessions
cards.description: Mental health support should work around you. Remote sessions offer confidential therapy on private video or telephone platforms. All service formats are available remotely, to provide full flexibility without compromising clinical quality.

workplace.heading: Workplace Therapy
workplace.body:
Mental health within the workplace is an often overlooked element of wellbeing. But this is an issue that has an impact on individuals and organisations. In 2024/25 over 900,000 workers experienced work-related stress, anxiety or depression - leading to the loss of 22.1 million working days Health and Safety Executive (2025). 
I have worked with companies such as LADBible and Genuit Group to provide therapy and support for their employees. My work with these companies has reduced absences related to mental health, supported appropriate returns-to-work, and improved employee retention.  

Employee feedback has highlighted positive impacts such as reduced stress and anxiety around work, improved relationships with colleagues and an appreciation for the human-focused culture their organisation has adopted. 

It is also vital that I work closely with the organisation, this allows managers and leaders to make referrals if they identify a member of the team who would benefit from therapy. It also allows me to liaise with HR to make recommendations regarding absent staff and supporting their return to work. My service remains confidential and I do not disclose details, but this collaboration means support is holistic and integrated into workplace culture. Another element of my work is mental health and wellbeing advocacy, so I often inform and advise organisations on how they can better support their employees and how best to implement the appropriate steps.

Organisations have reported increased productivity and outcomes from employees receiving therapy, less time lost to absences and more confidence in their ability to effectively support individuals in and out of work.

approach.heading: Therapeutic Approach
approach.intro: Grounded in evidence-based practice, I draw from several clinical frameworks to provide the most effective support for every individual and their circumstances.

items.title: Psychodynamic
items.description: Works with the understanding that present difficulties are influenced by unconscious processes and previous life experiences. Psychodynamic therapy creates space to explore your patterns, defence mechanisms and emotional history, and how these may impact you in the present.

items.title: Trauma-Informed
items.description: This framework prioritises sensitivity and collaborative sessions to acknowledge and address trauma and its role in mental health. There is a focus on creating a therapeutic environment that is safe, honest and understanding. You are the priority, and have control over the pace and direction of sessions, so the therapeutic work can provide effective support and empowerment.

items.title: Timeline Therapy
items.description: This technique is designed to support emotional and personal growth by identifying unconscious patterns of language and behaviour. The process aims to release limiting beliefs and emotional blocks to create lasting changes. The therapeutic work allows exploration of patterns by understanding the past, to being implementing positive change in the present and future. This may also include genograms to look into family dynamics and relationships.

items.title: Integrative
items.description: Integrative practice draws upon elements from many therapeutic frameworks (such as the systemic and humanistic approaches) to provide support tailored to each individual. Mental health support is not "one-size-fits-all" so the integrative approach can adapt to everyone.

approach.quote: "Out of your vulnerabilities will come your strength."

process.heading: The Process
process.intro: A clear, accessible and confidential pathway from initial contact to beginning therapy.

steps.title: Initial Enquiry
steps.description: Submit the contact form or send an email. All enquiries are treated with full discretion and responded to within a timely manner.

steps.title: Complimentary Consultation
steps.description: An initial consultation is a free 20-minute call for you to discuss your needs, ask me any questions, and establish whether I am the right clinician for you and your situation.

steps.title: Begin Treatment
steps.description: Sessions are scheduled at a suitable time for you. We will work together to identify your goals in therapy, set sustainable targets and review progress regularly.

contact.heading: Make an Enquiry
contact.intro: Complete the form below. All enquiries are strictly confidential.
contact.availability: No availability at present, but please do still get in touch as availability changes often.
contact.confidentialityText: All enquiries are handled with complete discretion. You are not obliged to share anything before you are ready - a name and a brief message is sufficient. Thank you!
